A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProDA and are readable, including equations, tables and figures. All 13 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v4 support comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references; v4 includes Appendices A–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original Charades recognition results, component ablations, prompt-robustness measurements and temporal-localization experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains those experiments and adds SportsHHI results, scene-disjoint Charades evaluation, feature-distance analysis and additional training-stage and qualitative results.

M1.justification: The core Charades architecture and losses remain unchanged. However, v4 adds a SportsHHI-specific implementation that augments the official baseline with DPM and AD Loss (Section 4.1). The appendix's fuller encoder and graph-parsing descriptions do not establish that the original Charades implementation changed.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates Charades using Action Genome annotations. v4 additionally evaluates human-human interaction classification on SportsHHI basketball and volleyball videos. Appendix D.1 also introduces evaluation on unseen Charades scene types, extending the tested environmental conditions.

E2.justification: The original Charades comparator set is retained. v4 Table 2 adds comparisons with STTran, HORT, SlowFast, ACARN, the SportsHHI baseline and an enlarged, approximately parameter-matched SportsHHI baseline. Table 11 additionally compares against STIGPN and LaIAR under scene shift.

E3.justification: v4 introduces SportsHHI evaluation with recall-at-K metrics and a capacity-matched control, plus five scene-disjoint Charades train/test configurations. Appendix D.2 also states that stage two trains only the a_t classifier, conflicting with the broader classifier training retained from v1 in Section 4.1. This changes the reported protocol description without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds a capacity control addressing model-size confounding, scene-shift tests of generalization, t-SNE and feature-distance analysis of class separation, and pre/post-training normalization and loss comparisons. Appendix E adds localization and graph-parsing case studies involving concurrent interactions. The original ablations and prompt-robustness analyses remain.

E5.justification: The same plus/minus reporting is retained for prompt robustness, with no newly specified seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added feature-distance summaries provide further descriptive results using plus/minus notation, rather than establishing a changed uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Original Charades scores, including ProDA's 71.1 mAP, are unchanged. New results include SportsHHI mAP of 13.55 versus 10.69 for the original baseline and 10.16 for its enlarged variant; scene-shift mAP of 63.0 versus LaIAR's 57.2 and STIGPN's 54.1; and pre-training results in Tables 12–13. Feature-distance measurements and parsing examples are also added. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies mathematical forms for edge-feature construction, scalar gating, weighted messages and node updates in Equations 9–12, beyond v1's prose description. The original Equations 1–8 remain unchanged. Appendix C's equations principally illustrate existing prompt rules; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain prompt-guided action disentanglement, state-of-the-art multi-label recognition and localization without localization supervision. The revised abstract names Charades and SportsHHI as supporting evaluations, but does not materially redefine those contributions. The conclusion is substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations attributing SportsHHI gains primarily to AD Loss rather than capacity, linking feature separation to discriminative representations, and explaining unseen-scene generalization through disentanglement. Appendix F newly identifies reliance on visual features and SSGs as a limitation when multimodal cues are needed. These substantially extend the interpretation and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Appendices A–D newly disclose encoder branches, MLP and attention implementations, cross-frame node correspondence and padding, concrete SAP/UAP examples, 16-frame inputs, five epochs per training stage, learning rates of 2e-4 and 1e-4, and checkpoint-selection rules. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although some training descriptions conflict with the main text. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references supporting SportsHHI, MultiSports, interaction baselines, STIGPN and t-SNE. These extend the comparison context, while the related-work taxonomy and positioning of action-conditioned disentanglement against existing representation methods remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Although much main-text prose is retained, Appendices A–C substantially expand the exposition through encoder, graph-parsing and worked prompt-construction explanations. The experimental narrative places benchmark comparisons before ablations and adds a visualization section, organized supplementary sections and a limitations discussion.

P2.justification: v4 adds the SportsHHI comparison, scene-split and domain-shift tables, and pre/post-training tables. New figures show t-SNE embeddings, encoder and attention architecture, localization examples and graph-parsing sequences. Existing figures and Charades tables are retained but several are relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens v1's Charades-only empirical support through SportsHHI evaluation with a capacity-matched control and scene-disjoint generalization tests. Its appendices also expose previously unspecified implementation and training choices. These improve validation and inspectability despite unchanged original scores. Conflicting stage-two descriptions and the insufficiently isolated attribution of SportsHHI gains to AD Loss limit clarity, but do not outweigh the substantial gains.
